items.payload: /spec:plan the CLIENT state, driver half (ADR-0010's unplanned state; brief 22a reserved 09 for it and that number went elsewhere). Carry: SIGNOFF becomes CLIENT between WALK and APPROVED; notes gain origin (walk|client|session) derived server-side from the entry route, NEVER from the typed 'by' field; APPROVED refuses while any client-origin note is open; clients see product-kind rows only, never process rows or the walk lane; 'notes address' refuses when the anchored screen file is unchanged since the note was raised (the cheap derived substitute for ADR-0010's before/after render, which is deferred to its own later spec, gated on a client asking for it); a ledgered waiver (reason recorded) releases APPROVED when a client goes quiet, or the whole project strands on one person. NO AUTH and no capability token (JJ 2026-09-09) — residual accepted: anyone holding the link can post or resolve as anyone. Testable without a browser; the served client view (whole-project entry, filtered view, reachability precondition on the exposed URL) is its own second spec.

review driver warns 'durable ledger row no longer readable' after drainStoppedRows moved the GATE_RED row into the main ledger on purpose — false alarm on every stopped-then-recovered review (seen on 20261101/11)
smoke-port test flakes under parallel runs: fixture bootCommand touches ready before trapping TERM, so an early SIGTERM exits 143 (seen in review rv_e028d73852e2)
spec 20261103/08: queue-side origin, trigger and batch fields so a lane-born fix names the lane that bore it (fanout-driver then admits depth-1 births by origin, not by after.spec)

review ESCALATE queue pick records laneExit in review-state.json then prints 'delete <sidecarDir>', so a fan-out lane following the step loses the laneExit --mark returned reads (specs/20261103/04 advisory a0)
policy.stops.rejectWithEvidence: auto-accept a disposer reject that carries an executed repro (needs a disposer return-shape field; sits beside 'only the user waives')

fix.md's waive/reject step never reads policy.stops.rejectWithEvidence, so /spec:fix asks about a finding the review driver would auto-accept on an executed repro; apply the same accept-on-repro rule (spec-review-driver.js ~1647), waives stay human

policy.stops.prototypeClose defaults to ask, so every prototype-backed spec close asks the same delete question; flip the default to delete (contract, pictures, tests survive under design/prototypes/<stem>/; branch reflog-recoverable) with a 📌 line, veto --prototype keep; also route the review driver's repair-round-spent exit through stops.reviewEscalate (queue) instead of leaving the session to choose

The fan-out leaves queued fix items and red-CI fixes out unless --include-fixes is passed, so a bare run (and every /clear resume) skips startable fix work the user expects drained; make the serial fix group the default with a 📌 line, replace the flag with an opt-out (--no-fixes), and update fanout.md, the driver's flag parsing and its tests

Opt-in interactive item picking for the fan-out: --pick prints the driver's candidate table, asks one multiSelect per chunk of 4 (max 16; beyond that only the first boundary window), and resolves to the existing --batch <ids> so the pick goes through the same boundary validation (self-surface, shared critical files, unmet dependencies) — never a silent --override-serial; confirm --batch itself re-applies those checks. A bare run stays automatic (📌 batch line); the pick is never written into queue order (spec-queue move exists for that)

Trim /spec:fanout to two modes, removing flags: a bare run is AUTO (derived batch in queue order, queued and red-CI fixes included as the serial fix group, one 📌 batch line, no question); /spec:fanout --pick is SELF-PICK (one multiSelect per chunk of 4 candidates, max 16, labelled in plain words, routed through the same boundary checks as auto — self-surface, shared critical files, unmet dependencies — never a bypass). Remove the user-facing --batch, --include-fixes, --override-serial, --ask, --lanes and positional spec paths unless a caller in the pipeline prints them (check spec-status --next, other commands, tests first; keep an internal driver flag only if --pick needs it). Net change should delete more doctrine and driver code than it adds; update fanout.md, the driver's flag parsing and its tests

Prove it: grep for each removed flag and field name returns nothing outside the changelog entry, and the diff deletes more lines than it adds

Repeated always-same asks outside the drivers: /spec:init policy rounds 1+2 (8 questions; write POLICY_DEFAULTS with one 📌 line per key, veto --ask-policy), init substrate create, init no-remote CI inert, init write-confirm when the dry-run shows no drift; /spec:plan critical 'lock it now?' (lock + 📌, veto --draft); /spec:fix authored-strings decisions stop (print as 📌 veto window, stops.fixDecisions); /spec:doctor --fix per-patch yes (apply all cited patches, veto --ask; test deletion stays human)

fanout-driver inspectReturned marks every /spec:fix lane 'stopped — returned without a recognised stop' because it requires a clean worktree, but /spec:fix appends its fix row to .claude/spec-runs.jsonl uncommitted after /git:commit (q29 lane, 2026-11-04); the merge step never runs and the fix row is lost with the worktree. Treat a dirty tree whose only change is spec-runs.jsonl appends as merge-ready and promote the rows at MERGE like spec lanes do

Fan-out lane worktrees are cut from a stale base (the harness worktree for spec 08 sat at 7558f342 after spec 06 merged as 00f8cd2a), so a lane builds on old code; the dispatch prompt's first command must fast-forward the lane branch to the main root's HEAD and refuse if it cannot. Also the build driver's preflight moves a spec to implementing while a depends_on spec is not done on the lane's base — refuse there with the remedy instead

tag sole-executor tests [invariant]: run the suite under --experimental-test-coverage once per test file, mark every test that is the only executor of a spec/scripts code path with [invariant] in its title, so the catch-up sweep under spec 13's keep rule keeps real guards; root cause: no existing test carries the tag the new keep rule reads

run the catch-up expiry sweep once under spec 13's keep rule, after the [invariant] tagging pass: node spec/scripts/expire-tests.js --root . --all-done --apply, commit the deletions, record tests and wall-clock before and after; root cause: ~1,150 AC-tagged tests of closed specs predate close-time expiry (replaces q26, whose gate was spec 20261103/05 and whose rule retired only 83)
